analysis:
The only change is a documentation addition in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 808-823). It describes parked 64 MiB paged KV segments retained after row release, the zero-fill-on-demand host-page wrapping, the reclaim triggers (refused admission, memory pressure, 30 s idle), and the env rollbacks DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0. No source, config or code changed in the supplied evidence, so no control was observed to regress.

Relevant threat IDs: T-028 (residual KV/GPU memory after a request completes) and T-014/T-011 (operator memory inspection). Parked segments that are reinstalled for the next same-size-class admission could hold a prior request's KV bytes. The documentation says new segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand pages, but it does not say whether reinstalled parked segments are scrubbed before reuse. Within a single provider process, T-028 already treats residual GPU memory as accepted/known, and the provider is already an adversarial-operator trust domain, so this is not a new disclosure to the operator. The risk for cross-consumer leakage would depend on paged attention masks and the lengths and ownership of reused segments. That logic is in EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift and PagedKVGroup.swift, which were not supplied. I cannot verify the implementation, so no finding is raised; this is an integration question.

Second question: parked backing sits outside the grant, floor and ledger charge, up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8). That is an availability or memory-accounting matter for the shared budget, not a documented threat here. The doc says it is dropped under memory pressure and on a refused charge. The implementation is not in evidence.

The prefix-cache threat T-041 is not touched: no SSD cache, TTL, key, or scope changes. Recommend that the code-side change reviewer confirm that reused parked segments cannot expose stale KV across requests or tenants, and that the unaccounted parked memory is bounded as documented.
